Guillermo's own take for Wed, Nov 25 (his read, quote it as his, not yours): The southeast storm is easing this morning. At 6am Sand Heads read SSE 17, down from 28 at 4am. Pam Rocks was S 15 gusting 24, a bit ahead of the page.

White Rock is already going and  Tsawwassen south side 8:15am to 1pm, SSE 19 to 20, tide above 11ft all day. Boundary Bay is the easier call, 9am to noon, SSE 14 to 15. Check before driving: if Sand Heads still reads SSE 15 or more at 7:30, go.  Erwin should also be on as Point Atkinson is already gusting 30 knots.  Wind should ease by noon and pick up my late afternoon again.

Rider weed reports (floating weed or eelgrass, last 3 days; mention them when suggesting these spots): Tsawwassen Ferry Terminal Causeway: lots of weed (Wed, Nov 25 10:00).

EC marine forecast, Howe Sound (issued 10:30 AM PCT 25 November 2026), WARNING IN EFFECT: Today Tonight and Thursday. Wind northerly outflow 5 to 15 knots except southeast 20 with gusts to 30 near the mouth of Howe Sound. Wind becoming northerly outflow 15 to 25 early this evening except southeast 30 with gusts to 40 near the mouth of Howe Sound tonight. Wind becoming southerly inflow 10 to 15 Thursday morning. Strong wind warning program has ended for the season.

EC marine forecast, Strait of Georgia (south of Nanaimo) (issued 10:30 AM PCT 25 November 2026), WARNING IN EFFECT: Today Tonight and Thursday. Gale warning in effect. Wind southeast 20 to 25 knots increasing to southeast 30 to 35 early this evening except southeast 35 to 45 south of Tsawwassen. Wind becoming southeast 30 late overnight then veering to southwest 25 near noon Thursday. Wind diminishing to southwest 15 to 20 Thursday afternoon then backing to southerly 15 Thursday evening. Strong wind warning program has ended for the season.
